title: This Chinese Frame Feels More Premium Than Most Western Brands

takeaways.text: Frame sent by Yoeleo for review (affiliate link). The frame weighed 1.33 kg with hanger, bash guard and covers (storage bags removed); bar 390 g, fork 490 g, seatpost 172 g, thru-axles about 70 g, metal out-front mount 41 g. Frame size was not stated.
Bottom-bracket shell, brake mounts and headset seats were faced and clean, with only a small paint lip near the BB; the interior carbon visible through the storage ports looked very clean.
He describes it as a US$1,400 frameset (August 2026).

2.1 in Schwalbe Thunder Burt tires left plenty of room front and rear; he thinks 2.2–2.25 in would fit. A 46T 1× ring was tight with a standard spindle; he cites Yoeleo's 44T limit (other reviewers quote 42T).
Dislikes: the in-frame bags hold little and are slow to access mid-race, and the integrated bar comes in few sizes with a wide flare; the round seatpost allows suspension or dropper posts.
The race-ready SRAM Rival XPLR AXS build with Yoeleo wheels, power-meter crank, pedals and cages weighed 8.78 kg.

disclosure: The description says Yoeleo sent the frame and includes a 10% discount code.
summary: Gravel racer's full build with weights, tire clearance, finish and seatpost compatibility, ending at an 8.78 kg race-ready bike before a three-week race block.
